findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword the opcert_from_record docstring so it does not claim that all callers verify on the embedded key: name verify_opcert_record (validity, plus the trust list when one is set) and verify_completion_opcert (trust list required), and note that some callers only read the bound fields.
evidence: Plan: "the production consumer `verify_opcert_record` (`src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py:170`) verifies it on the key embedded in its signature"
Plan proposed text: "Callers verify the returned envelope on the key embedded in its signature (verify_opcert_record, ADR 0125)"
Searching for `opcert_from_record(` finds callers at _opcert_verify.py:192, llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:193, opcert_service/jobs.py:158 and _commands/verify_opcert.py:76
bugfix_size_gate.py:181: "the signing principal is deliberately NOT consulted", so it decodes without verifying
_commands/verify_opcert.py:92 calls verify_completion_opcert(..., required_env=..., trusted_pairs=...), which returns `untrusted` unless the pair is listed (_opcert_verify.py:341-350)
findings.finding: The plan calls verify_opcert_record 'the production consumer' of opcert_from_record, and the replacement docstring generalizes from that ('Callers verify the returned envelope on the key embedded in its signature (verify_opcert_record, ADR 0125)'). In fact opcert_from_record has 4 callers that use it differently. _commands/verify_opcert.py passes the envelope to verify_completion_opcert, which requires a trust list. llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py deliberately never checks the signer and reads only the bound fields. opcert_service/jobs.py only attaches the envelope. So the new docstring would make an over-broad claim of its own.
findings.location: Approach — `attest/opcert.py:348` bullet; Context bullet on `opcert.py:348` ('the production consumer verify_opcert_record')
scenarios: A developer reads the new docstring and assumes every caller verifies the signature, then reuses opcert_from_record in a gate that trusts the bound fields without verifying them, as bugfix_size_gate already does on purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with: "Verifying callers check the returned envelope on the key embedded in its signature (ADR 0125): verify_opcert_record checks validity, plus verify.trusted_opcert_keys when that list is set, and the merge gate's verify_completion_opcert requires a listed (environment, key) pair; :func:`verify_opcert` stays the keyed-era primitive."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the AC3 pattern for opcert.py:6 match the actual source text (e.g. plain `out-of-band-pinned`), and confirm it matches the pre-fix line before relying on it.
evidence: AC3: "-e 'out-of-band-pinned\*\* public'"
Context: "says anyone verifies an op-cert \"against that environment's out-of-band-pinned public key\"" (no asterisks quoted)
findings.finding: AC3's pattern `'out-of-band-pinned\*\* public'` matches only the literal text `out-of-band-pinned** public`. In git grep's default basic regex, `\*` is a literal asterisk. The plan's own quotation of the target docstring is `out-of-band-pinned public key`, with no asterisks. If the source matches that quotation, the pattern never matches before or after the fix. That half of the AC then passes vacuously and does not prove the opcert.py:6 edit landed.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, third item (git grep with -e 'out-of-band-pinned\*\* public')
scenarios: The implementer forgets to edit attest/opcert.py:6. AC3 still prints nothing because the escaped-asterisk pattern never matched the plain text, so the stale docstring ships while the AC reads green.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `-e 'out-of-band-pinned\*\* public'` with `-e 'out-of-band-pinned'`. This matches both the plain and bold-marked forms. Then confirm it prints `src/rebar/attest/opcert.py:6` on the pre-fix tree.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the re-identify warning rewrite (env_identity.py ~176), state that `verify.require_environment` requires a `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` list naming that environment's keys, as well as turning certs from other environments `foreign_key`.
evidence: Approach summary: "`verify.require_environment` turns a certificate naming another environment `foreign_key` and requires a trust list."
Warning bullet: "`verify.require_environment` turns a certificate naming another environment `foreign_key`." (no trust-list requirement)

src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py:260-271: `if required_env is not None and not with_list:` returns verdict `foreign_key` with reason '... requires a verify.trusted_opcert_keys list naming that environment's keys (ADR 0125)'

The current warning text ('trusts only the own or pinned keys of the environment it names') at least signals that require_environment narrows trust to listed keys. The planned text loses that restriction.
findings.finding: The planned rewrite of the re-identify warning says only that `verify.require_environment` turns a certificate naming another environment `foreign_key`. It leaves out that `require_environment` also needs a `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` list. Without that list, the verifier returns `foreign_key` for every certificate, including ones naming the required environment. The plan's own summary of the model includes this rule ('and requires a trust list'), but the warning text does not.
scenarios: An operator re-clones and then sets `verify.require_environment` to the old environment id so that old attestations count, without setting a trust list. Following the new warning, they expect old certs to verify. Instead every cert, old and new, reads `foreign_key`.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the warning bullet to something like: "`verify.require_environment` turns a certificate naming another environment `foreign_key`, and requires a `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` list naming that environment's keys (without one, every op-cert reads `foreign_key`)."
